messages:
morgan: Heads-up folks — two incidents where dedicated pools didn't satisfy burst requests because nodes were still provisioning. First-request latency spiked ~7s.
raj: saw that in telemetry. slow device attestation + kubelet join was the blocker, right?
claire: yep. plus our runtime needs ~2-5s to warm model cache after node Ready. So total cold-path ~10s often.
morgan: thinking we should split "admit" (fast decision) from "reconciler" (slow placement). Admit issues a temp lease quickly; reconciler commits after verifying node+model-ready.
jordan: split reduces latency for successful fast-fits but adds async failure modes. what are we protecting against?
morgan: main fail modes: (A) admit grants lease but reconciler never commits -> stuck token; (B) reconciler duplicates prewarms; (C) retries thrash cloud quotas.
raj: mitigate (A) with short temp_lease_ttl (10s) and an extend-on-commit flow. If no commit before ttl we reclaim tokens and surface metrics.
claire: for (B) reconciler should try soft-fit onto existing warm nodes first (LRU by last-primed-model) before creating new node. tag attempts to avoid duplicates.
morgan: propose admit returns {allowed, lease_id, ttl_s}. clients get immediate yes/no and can fallback to alternate route if no commit within 3s. recommender uses commit_window=15s to finish slow path.
raj: cloud create calls need exponential backoff + jitter. client retry policy should be gentler (linear small increments) so UX doesn't oscillate. Separate throttles for tenant-initiated vs infra-initiated prewarms.
claire: config sketch:
```yaml
admit:
  temp_lease_ttl: "10s"
  commit_window: "15s"
  client_retry_policy:
    initial: "300ms"
    max: "2s"
  provision_backoff:
    base: "500ms"
    multiplier: 2.0
    max: "5s"
  circuit_breaker:
    fail_threshold: 5
    reset_after: "30s"
```
morgan: metrics to add: temp_lease_grants, temp_lease_expiries, commit_success_rate, commit_latency_p50/p95, provision_api_errors, prewarm_throttle_drops. Alert if commit_success_rate < 95% in 5m.
jordan: rollout plan: feature-flagged admit_split off by default. Canary on a low-volume tenant. Add synthetic that simulates slow kube join to validate TTL reclaim.
raj: cleanup: tag any cloud resources with lease_id; if reconciler misses commit window, async cleanup job must release resources to prevent ghost nodes and cloud spend.
claire: cost control: cap burst-prewarms by tenant credit bucket. reconciler should prefer reusing partial-capacity nodes. also region-level tunables for backoff (old regions slower).
morgan: tests: unit TTL/extend/expiry, reconciler commit race tests, e2e with fake-cloud (slow-join, provisioning-error, success). stress test high-churn tenants.
jordan: API surface minimal: POST /admit -> {allowed: bool, lease_id: string|null, ttl_s: int, reason: string?}. POST /commit {lease_id} -> {ok: bool, error: string?}.
raj: one caveat: leases that frequently expire might indicate headroom miscalc; add headroom_adjustment_metric and autosignal to reduce admit rate.
claire: ops-bot: created ticket INF-3912 for implementation + dashboards. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Ticket INF-3912 created by claire — "Admit/Reconciler split + temp-lease/backoff policy" Priority: P2
morgan: i'll start a branch with an admit proto and small fake-cloud harness. tagging @raj @claire for review.
jordan: i'll draft a short RFC addendum describing failure modes, configs, and rollout steps.
morgan: thanks. let's keep the admit surface small and observable.
claire: ack, moving to follow-up PRs. :rocket:
